## The Corn Islands in the Caribbean Sea

The Corn Islands lie in the Caribbean Sea, not far from Nicaragua's coast. In earlier times the islands bustled with pirates who sought refuge here and spent their plunder. Today, a quiet, unhurried island life prevails.

## The Corn Islands for Nature Lovers!

Parts of the local flora and fauna have survived here since pre-Columbian times. On Big Corn Island, you can look forward to a relaxed holiday, excellent fishing, the wonders of the underwater world and powdery white-sand beaches. The uninhabited Little Corn Island, with its sandy beaches, is a place where sea turtles lay their eggs. Reefs surround the islands, alive with marine creatures. Slip beneath the surface and discover their beauty: the underwater world is so captivating that you may forget everything else.

Otavalo is the capital of the canton of the same name in Ecuador. The city has more than 60,000 residents. Indigenous peoples inhabited these lands some 10,000 years ago, long before Spanish colonisation.

The city museum displays clothing, tableware, tools and other objects connected with local customs and everyday life.

Otavalo's main attraction is its handicraft market. Local artisans work with textiles and pass their skills down from generation to generation. At the height of the season, market stalls occupy a significant part of the city.

The Saturday market in Plaza de los Ponchos is particularly famous. Here you can see traditional clothing worn by local people and buy textiles, blankets, tablecloths and other souvenirs.

Tiradentes Square remains one of the main starting points for a walk through Ouro Preto. From here, it is easy to continue along historic streets to museums and religious monuments. You can devote a separate part of your trip to the old gold mines, which reveal another side of the region's history.

On a longer itinerary through Brazil, Ouro Preto combines well with Rio de Janeiro and an onward flight via Belo Horizonte. This makes it possible to add a dedicated historical stop to a journey covering major cities and natural regions.

### Lake Yojoa — The Largest Lake in Honduras!

Lake Yojoa is the largest lake in Honduras, covering 285 square kilometres. Formed by volcanic activity, it has water lilies along its shores and is home to around four hundred bird species.

## Relaxing at Lake Yojoa

### Lake Yojoa — A Wonderful Place to Unwind!

The lake lies beside the highway connecting Honduras's two largest cities, Tegucigalpa and San Pedro Sula. This makes it a convenient place to stop and relax while travelling between them. You can enjoy views of the lake and sample freshly fried fish at the restaurants along its shores. The spectacular cascading Pulhapanzak Falls are also easy to reach. National parks with rich flora and fauna lie on the lake's western and eastern shores.
